metadata.source: Yutaka Iwamoto: Kleinere Dhāraṇī Texte, Kyoto 1937 (Beiträge zur Indologie, 2), pp. 1-6.

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / śītavane mahāśmaśāne iṅghikāyatanapratyuddeśe tatrāyuṣmān rāhulo 'tīva viheṭhyate / devagrahair nāgagrahair yakṣagrahai rākṣagrahair marutagrahair asuragrahair kinnaragrahair garuḍagrahair gandharvagrahair mahoragagrahair manuṣyagrahair amanuṣyagrahair pretagrahair bhūtagrahair piśācagrahair kumbhāṇḍagrahair dvīpibhiḥ kākair ulūkaiḥ kīṭaiḥ sarīsṛpair anyaiś ca manuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ satvaiḥ / athāyuṣmān rāhulo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ purato rudann aśrūṇi pravartayati sma /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Śītavana</s> (Cool Grove), the great charnel ground, near the <s>Iṅghikā</s> shrine. There the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> was exceedingly tormented by <s>deva</s>-seizures, <s>nāga</s>-seizures, <s>yakṣa</s>-seizures, <s>rākṣasa</s>-seizures, <s>maruta</s>-seizures, <s>asura</s>-seizures, <s>kinnara</s>-seizures, <s>garuḍa</s>-seizures, <s>gandharva</s>-seizures, <s>mahoraga</s>-seizures, human-seizures, non-human-seizures, <s>preta</s>-seizures, <s>bhūta</s>-seizures, <s>piśāca</s>-seizures, <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>-seizures, leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other human and non-human beings. Then the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> approached the Blessed One, and having approached, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated the Blessed One three times, and standing before the Blessed One, began to weep and shed tears.

body.text: atha bhagavān jānann eva rāhulam āmantrayate sma / kiṃ tvaṃ rāhula mama prataḥ sthitvā aśrūṇi pravartayasi / evam ukte āyuṣmān rāhulo bhagavantam etad avocat / ihāhaṃ bhagavan rājagṛhe viharāmi śītavane mahāśmaśāne iṅghikāyatanapratyuddeśe (

children.text: ) so 'haṃ bhagavaṃs tatra viheṭhye / devagrahair nāgagrahair yakṣagrahai rākṣasagrahair marutagrahair asuragrahair kinnaragrahair garuḍagrahair gandharvagrahair mahoragagrahair manuṣyagrahair amanuṣyagrahair pretagrahair bhūtagrahair piśācagrahair kumbhāṇḍagrahair dvīpibhiḥ kākair ulūkaiḥ kīṭaiḥ sarīsṛpair anyaiś ca manuṣyāmanuṣyaiḥ satvaiḥ //
children.translated_text: And there, Blessed One, I am tormented by <s>deva</s>-seizures, <s>nāga</s>-seizures, <s>yakṣa</s>-seizures, <s>rākṣasa</s>-seizures, <s>maruta</s>-seizures, <s>asura</s>-seizures, <s>kinnara</s>-seizures, <s>garuḍa</s>-seizures, <s>gandharva</s>-seizures, <s>mahoraga</s>-seizures, human-seizures, non-human-seizures, <s>preta</s>-seizures, <s>bhūta</s>-seizures, <s>piśāca</s>-seizures, <s>kumbhāṇḍa</s>-seizures, leopards, crows, owls, insects, reptiles, and other human and non-human beings.'

body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, knowing [the cause], addressed <s>Rāhula</s>: 'Why, <s>Rāhula</s>, do you stand before me shedding tears?' When thus addressed, the venerable <s>Rāhula</s> said this to the Blessed One: 'Here I am, Blessed One, dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Śītavana</s>, the great charnel ground, near the <s>Iṅghikā</s> shrine.

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ rāhulam āmantrayate sma / udgṛhṇa tvaṃ rāhula imāṃ mahāśītavatī nāma dhāraṇīṃ vidyāṃ / catasṛṇāṃ pariṣadāṃ rakṣāvaraṇaguptaye bhikṣūṇāṃ bhikṣuṇīnām upāsakānām upāsikānāṃ ca sarvasatvānāṃ ca dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya yogakṣemāya bhaviṣyati //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>: 'Take up, <s>Rāhula</s>, this <s>dhāraṇī</s> <s>vidyā</s> (protective spell) called <s>Mahāśītavatī</s>. It will serve for the long-lasting benefit, welfare, happiness, and security of the four assemblies — <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>upāsakas</s>, and <s>upāsikās</s> — and of all beings, for their protection, warding, and safeguarding.'

body.text: tadyathā / aṅgā vaṅgā / kaliṅga / varaṅgā saṃsārataraṅgā sāsadaṅgā / bhagā asurā / ekataraṅgā asuravīrā / tara vīrā / tara tara vīrā / kara vīrā / kara kara vīrā / indrā indrakisarā / haṃsā haṃsakisarā / picimālā / mahākiccā / viheṭhikā kālucchikā / aṅgodara jayālikā / velā cintāli / cili cili hili hili sumati vasumati / culu naṭṭe / culu culu naṭṭe / culu culu culu naṭṭe / culu nāḍi / (

children.text: ) ku nāḍi / hārīṭaki hārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki / gauri gandhāri / caṇḍāli vetāli / mātaṅgi / varcasi dharaṇi dhāṛaṇi / taraṇi tāraṇi / uṣṭramālike / kaca kācike / kaca kācive / cala nāṭike / kākalike / lalamati / lakṣamati / varāhakule / matpale utpale / kara vīre / kara kara vīre / tara vīre / tara tara vīre / kuru vīre / kuru kuru vīre / curu vīre / curu curu vīre / mahāvīre / iramati / varamati / rakṣamati / sarvārthasādhani / paramārthasādhani / apratihate / indro rājā / yamo rājā / varuṇo rājā / kubero rājā / manasvī rājā / vāsukī rājā / daṇḍakī rājā / daṇḍāgnī rājā / dhṛtarāṣṭro rājā / virūḍhako rājā / virūpākṣo rājā / brahmā sahasrādhipatī rājā / buddho bhagavān dharmasvāmī rājā / anuttaro lokānukaṃpakaḥ / mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ karotu /
children.translated_text: <s>ku nāḍi / hārīṭaki hārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki kārīṭaki / gauri gandhāri / caṇḍāli vetāli / mātaṅgi / varcasi dharaṇi dhāraṇi / taraṇi tāraṇi / uṣṭramālike / kaca kācike / kaca kācive / cala nāṭike / kākalike / lalamati / lakṣamati / varāhakule / matpale utpale / kara vīre / kara kara vīre / tara vīre / tara tara vīre / kuru vīre / kuru kuru vīre / curu vīre / curu curu vīre / mahāvīre / iramati / varamati / rakṣamati / sarvārthasādhani / paramārthasādhani / apratihate /</s> <s>Indra</s> is king! <s>Yama</s> is king! <s>Varuṇa</s> is king! <s>Kubera</s> is king! <s>Manasvī</s> is king! <s>Vāsukī</s> is king! <s>Daṇḍakī</s> is king! <s>Daṇḍāgni</s> is king! <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> is king! <s>Virūḍhaka</s> is king! <s>Virūpākṣa</s> is king! <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of a thousand [worlds], is king! The <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, the Lord of the <s>Dharma</s>, is king! The unsurpassed one, compassionate toward the world — may he grant protection for me and for all beings!

children.text: paritrāṇaṃ parigrahaṃ paripālanaṃ śāntiṃ svastyayanaṃ daṇḍaparihāraṃ śastraparihāraṃ
children.translated_text: safeguarding, embrace, watching over, peace, well-being, the warding off of punishment, the warding off of weapons,

children.text: viṣanāśanaṃ sīmābandhaṃ dharaṇībandhaṃ ca kurvantu jīvantu varṣaśataṃ paśyantu śaradāṃ śataṃ //
children.translated_text: the destruction of poison, the binding of the boundary, and the binding of the earth! May they live and see a hundred years, may they see a hundred autumns!

body.translated_text: The <s>dhāraṇī</s> is as follows: <s>aṅgā vaṅgā / kaliṅga / varaṅgā saṃsārataraṅgā sāsadaṅgā / bhagā asurā / ekataraṅgā asuravīrā / tara vīrā / tara tara vīrā / kara vīrā / kara kara vīrā / indrā indrakisarā / haṃsā haṃsakisarā / picimālā / mahākiccā / viheṭhikā kālucchikā / aṅgodara jayālikā / velā cintāli / cili cili hili hili sumati vasumati / culu naṭṭe / culu culu naṭṭe / culu culu culu naṭṭe / culu nāḍi /</s>

body.text: tadyathā / ilā milā utpalā / iramati viramati / halamati

children.text: / lakṣamati / rakṣamati / kuru kuru mati / huru huru phuru phuru cara (
children.translated_text: <s>lakṣamati / rakṣamati / kuru kuru mati / huru huru phuru phuru cara</s> (

children.text: ) cara khara khara khuru khuru mati mati bhūmicaṇḍe / kālike / abhisaṃlāpite / sāmalate / hūle sthūle / sthūlaśikhare / jaya sthūle / jayavate / vala naṭṭe / cara nāḍi culu nāḍi culu nāḍi vāgbandhani / virohaṇi / sālohite / aṇḍare paṇḍare / karāle / kinnare / keyūre ketumati / bhūtaṃgame bhūtamati / dhanye maṅgalye / hiraṇyagarbhe / mahābale / avalokitamūle / acalacaṇḍe / dhurandhare jayālike jayāgorohiṇi / curu curu phuru phuru rundha rundha dhare dhare vidhare vidhare viṣkambhani / nāśani vināśani / bandhani / mokṣaṇi vimokṣani / mocani vimocani / mohani vimohani / bhāvani vibhāvani / śodhani śodhani saṃśodhani viśodhani / saṃkhiraṇi / saṃkiraṇi / saṃcchindani / sādhu turamāṇe / hara hara bandhumati / hiri hiri khiri khiri kharali / huru huru khuru khuru piṅgale namo 'stu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: ) <s>cara khara khara khuru khuru mati mati bhūmicaṇḍe / kālike / abhisaṃlāpite / sāmalate / hūle sthūle / sthūlaśikhare / jaya sthūle / jayavate / vala naṭṭe / cara nāḍi culu nāḍi culu nāḍi vāgbandhani / virohaṇi / sālohite / aṇḍare paṇḍare / karāle / kinnare / keyūre ketumati / bhūtaṃgame bhūtamati / dhanye maṅgalye / hiraṇyagarbhe / mahābale / avalokitamūle / acalacaṇḍe / dhurandhare jayālike jayāgorohiṇi / curu curu phuru phuru rundha rundha dhare dhare vidhare vidhare viṣkambhani / nāśani vināśani / bandhani / mokṣaṇi vimokṣani / mocani vimocani / mohani vimohani / bhāvani vibhāvani / śodhani śodhani saṃśodhani viśodhani / saṃkhiraṇi / saṃkiraṇi / saṃcchindani / sādhu turamāṇe / hara hara bandhumati / hiri hiri khiri khiri kharali / huru huru khuru khuru piṅgale</s> — Homage to the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text: The [continued] <s>dhāraṇī</s>: <s>ilā milā utpalā / iramati viramati / halamati</s>

body.text: asyāṃ khalu punā rāhula mahāśītavatīvidyāyāṃ daśottarapadaśatāyāṃ sūtre granthiṃ baddhvā hastena dhāryamānāyāṃ kaṇṭhena dhāryamānāyāṃ samantād yojanaśatasya rakṣākṛtā bhaviṣyati (

children.text: ) / gandhair vā puṣpair vā mudrābhir vā naiva manuṣyo vāmanuṣyo vābhibhaviṣyati / na śastraṃ na viṣaṃ na rogo na jvaro na prajvaro na vidyāmantro na vetāḍaḥ / na vyādhinā nāgninā na viṣodakena kālaṃ kariṣyati / vidyāmantraprayogānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ sādhuprayuktānāṃ cāsiddhānāṃ siddhakarī / siddhānāṃ ca saṃkṣobhaṇī / paraprayuktānāṃ ca bandhanī / parabandhanānāṃ ca pramocanī / sarvarogaśokavighnavināyakānāṃ vināśanakarī / kalikalahakaluṣapraśamanakarī / yo graho na muñcet saptadhāsya sphuṭen mūrdhā arjakasyeva mañjarī / vajrapāṇiś cāsya mahāyakṣasenāpatir vajreṇādīptena prajvālitena ekajvālībhūtena tāvad vyāyacched yāvan mūrdhānaṃ sphoṭayet / catvāraś ca mahārājāno 'yomayena cakreṇa mūrdhānaṃ sphoṭayeyuḥ / kṣuradhārāprahāreṇa vināśayeyus tasmāc ca yakṣalokācyavanaṃ bhaveyuḥ / aḍakavatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ na labhate vāsam //
children.translated_text: ). Neither by perfumes, nor by flowers, nor by <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures) shall any human or non-human being overpower [the bearer]. Neither weapon, nor poison, nor disease, nor fever, nor burning fever, nor a <s>vidyā-mantra</s>, nor a <s>vetāḍa</s> (zombie) [shall harm them]. One shall not die by disease, nor by fire, nor by poisoned water. For all <s>vidyā-mantra</s> applications, even those well-employed that have not been accomplished, it brings accomplishment. For those already accomplished, it causes disruption [of hostile spells]. For those employed by others, it binds [them]. For those bound by others, it liberates. It destroys all diseases, sorrows, obstacles, and <s>Vināyakas</s> (obstructors). It pacifies strife, quarrel, and defilement. Whatever spirit does not release [the victim], his head shall split in seven pieces, like the flower-cluster of a <s>arjaka</s> (basil) plant. And <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>, the great commander of the <s>yakṣas</s>, shall strike with his <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt)—blazing, burning, become a single flame—until he splits [the spirit's] head. And the four Great Kings shall split its head with an iron wheel. They shall destroy it with the blow of a razor's edge, and it shall fall from the <s>yakṣa</s> world. It shall not find dwelling in the royal city of <s>Aḍakavatī</s>.

body.translated_text: Now furthermore, <s>Rāhula</s>, when this great <s>Mahāśītavatī vidyā</s>, this <s>sūtra</s> of one hundred and ten verses, is held in the hand with a knot tied, or worn around the neck, protection shall be made for a hundred <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) in all directions (

body.text: atha khalu punā rāhula mahāśītavatīmahāvidyāyāṃ sakṛtparivartitāyāṃ rājacaurodakāgniviṣaśastrāṭavīkāntāramadhyagataḥ sarvabhayebhyaḥ parimucyate / iyaṃ khalu punar mahāśītavatī vidyā (

children.text: ) ekanavatyāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāsamair buddhair bhagavadbhir bhāṣitā bhāṣiṣyate bhāṣyate ca siddhā paramasiddhā siddhaparākramā / sarvadevanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragādibhir vanditvā sarvajinagaṇaparivṛtā / sarvabhayopadraveṣu mama sarvasatvānāṃ ca rakṣāṃ kuru / śivam ārogyam abhayaṃ ca sarvadā sarvathā sarvataḥ sarvāvasthāsu bhavantu //
children.translated_text: ) was spoken, will be spoken, and is being spoken by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavats</s> as numerous as the sands of ninety-one <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers—accomplished, supremely accomplished, of accomplished power, venerated by all <s>devas</s>, <s>nāgas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, <s>kinnaras</s>, <s>mahoragas</s>, and the like, surrounded by the hosts of all Conquerors. Grant protection for me and for all sentient beings in all fears and calamities! May there be well-being, health, and fearlessness—always, in every way, everywhere, in all conditions!

body.translated_text: Now furthermore, <s>Rāhula</s>, when this great <s>Mahāśītavatī mahāvidyā</s> has been recited even once, one who has entered among dangers of kings, thieves, water, fire, poison, weapons, and wilderness is freed from all fears. And furthermore, this great <s>Mahāśītavatī vidyā</s> (

body.text: idam avocat bhagavān āttamanā āyuṣmān rāhulaḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhabhāṣitam abhyanandann iti //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the <s>Bhagavat</s>, with gladdened mind. The venerable <s>Rāhula</s> and that entire assembly, and the whole world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoiced in the well-spoken words of the <s>Bhagavat</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One.
The Noble <s>Mahāśītavatī</s>, the Queen of <s>Vidyās</s>, is completed.
